5.11 Embryo-Fetal Toxicity Based on human data, rituximab-containing products can cause fetal harm due to B-cell lymphocytopenia in infants exposed to rituximab in-utero. Advise pregnant women of the potential risk to a fetus. Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment with RITUXAN HYCELA and for 12 months after the last dose

tier.note: Human data demonstrate fetal harm (neonatal B-cell lymphocytopenia lasting <6 months) following in-utero exposure; requires baseline pregnancy testing and effective contraception during treatment and for 12 months after the last dose.

pregnancy_pk.value: Crosses placenta and is detected postnatally in infant serum; postmarketing human data show in-utero exposure causes neonatal B-cell lymphocytopenia generally lasting < 6 months. Observe newborns for signs of infection.

refs.quote: Postmarketing data indicate that B-cell lymphocytopenia generally lasting less than 6 months can occur in infants exposed to rituximab in-utero. Rituximab was detected postnatally in the serum of infants exposed in-utero.

contraception.value: Verify pregnancy status prior to initiating therapy; use effective contraception during treatment and for 12 months after the last dose.

lactation_summary.value: Excreted at low concentrations in human breast milk; advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 6 months after the last dose due to potential for serious adverse reactions in breastfed children.
